propositions: git fetch hangs indefinitely on byte-starved connections because _fetch_origin builds git argv without http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime, leaving only a 300s wall-clock timeout as the abort trigger
a stalled git fetch (connection accepted but zero bytes transferred) must abort in ~10 seconds via throughput-keyed abort rather than burning the full 300s budget
legitimately slow but progressing fetches (e.g., 90-second full clone of 80 MB repo) must not be aborted, requiring throughput floor rather than wall-time keying
transient low-speed aborts must be retried in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal within a single review, while non-low-speed failures (auth, bad ref) must not be retried
repo_snapshot.py module extraction into git_fetch.py is required due to 800 LOC module-size cap, moving git-subprocess and fetch-locking cluster along existing seam
